name: USB mouse (low-speed HID boot mouse)
description: A wired USB mouse on its cable: a low-speed HID device of the boot mouse protocol (three buttons, X, Y and a wheel), bus powered. Its inputs move it and press its buttons; a host (a computer's port, a microcontroller's USB host) enumerates it and polls its reports.

pins.name: VBUS
pins.doc: VBUS from the host: it attaches while VBUS is above 4.4 V

pins.name: DP
pins.doc: D+: the host on this net is the one it talks to

inputs.name: move_x
inputs.doc: Counts to move along X (right positive), added to what is still to send

inputs.name: move_y
inputs.doc: Counts to move along Y (down positive)

inputs.name: wheel
inputs.doc: Wheel detents (away from the user positive)

inputs.name: buttons
inputs.doc: The buttons held: bit 0 left, 1 right, 2 middle

outputs.name: idle_ms
outputs.doc: The idle rate SET_IDLE set (0: reports only on change)

functional.claims: A low-speed USB 2.0 device (D- pulled up) with chapter 9's standard requests (GET_DESCRIPTOR, SET_ADDRESS in effect after its status stage, SET/GET_CONFIGURATION, GET_STATUS, SET/CLEAR_FEATURE for remote wakeup and endpoint halt, GET/SET_INTERFACE), EP0 in 8-byte packets, data toggles per endpoint, attached while VBUS is above 4.4 V; HID 1.11's boot mouse: its HID and report descriptors, GET_REPORT, GET/SET_IDLE (an idle report every duration), GET/SET_PROTOCOL, an interrupt IN endpoint of 4 bytes polled every 10 ms that answers with a report when the buttons or the movement changed (at most 127 counts each way a report), NAK otherwise.
omissions: its supply current from VBUS (a mouse's 20 to 100 mA)
remote wakeup signalling (a button press on a suspended bus)
an optical sensor's resolution and acceleration: the movement is the inputs' counts

sources.title: Device Class Definition for Human Interface Devices (HID), Version 1.11 (USB-IF, 2001)
sources.notes: The boot mouse (appendix B.2), its report descriptor (appendix E.10), the class requests (7.2).

sources.title: Universal Serial Bus Specification, Revision 2.0 (USB-IF, 2000): chapter 9
sources.notes: The standard requests and descriptors, low-speed EP0's 8-byte packets.
